paragraphs.title: The Sword Drawn from Its Sheath

easy.explanation: Ezekiel is told to set his face toward Jerusalem and prophesy against the land of Israel.
easy.q: To whom is Ezekiel told to prophesy?

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I will draw forth my sword out of his sheath.”
easy.q: What will the Lord draw forth from its sheath?

easy.explanation: The prophecy says the sword will cut off both the righteous and the wicked.
easy.q: Whom will the sword cut off?

answers: From the south to the north
From the east to the west
medium.explanation: The sword goes against all flesh “from the south to the north.”
medium.q: In what direction will the sword go against all flesh?

answers: The sword is unsheathed and ready for use
The sword has been hidden permanently
medium.explanation: The phrase pictures a sword being removed from its sheath for judgment.
medium.q: What does the phrase “drawn forth out of his sheath” mean?

answers: That the Lord has drawn forth His sword
That the king of Babylon has fled
medium.explanation: All flesh will know that the Lord has drawn forth His sword.

answers: The Lord announces real judgment, while the people fail to recognize its seriousness
The Lord promises peace, while the people prepare for war
The Lord praises the people, while they reject the temple
challenge.explanation: The passage presents the sword as a real and unavoidable act of judgment.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the Lord’s warning and the people’s response implied in this passage?

answers: The judgment will spread broadly across the land
The sword will remain in one city
The sword will return immediately to its sheath
challenge.explanation: The directional movement emphasizes the wide reach of the judgment.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the sword’s movement from south to north?

answers: A command to prophesy, the sword drawn, judgment announced, and universal recognition
A feast, a coronation, and a military victory
A temple dedication followed by peace
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from Ezekiel’s commission to the drawing of the sword and its consequences.

paragraphs.title: The Sword Turned Against the Land

easy.explanation: Ezekiel is told to sigh with the breaking of his loins and with bitterness.
easy.q: What is Ezekiel commanded to do before the people?

answers: He will tell them about the coming tidings
He will deny that anything is wrong
He will tell them the war is over
easy.explanation: He must answer that the tidings are coming.
easy.q: What will happen when the people ask why he sighs?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “every heart shall melt.”
easy.q: What will happen to every heart?

answers: They will be lifted in victory
medium.explanation: The people’s hands will be feeble because of the coming disaster.
medium.q: What will happen to all hands?

medium.explanation: The expression describes sorrowful and painful mourning.
The passage says, “all knees shall be weak as water.”
medium.q: How are the people’s knees described?

answers: It visibly represents the grief and terror of the coming judgment
It announces that the people have won
It shows that the sword has been returned
challenge.explanation: His public sighing demonstrates the sorrow that the coming tidings will cause.
challenge.q: Why is Ezekiel’s sighing an important prophetic sign?

answers: It mentions the heart, hands, spirit, and knees failing
It describes only one frightened soldier
It says the people will remain completely calm
challenge.explanation: Several parts of the body and inner life are described as weakening.
challenge.q: How does the passage intensify the description of fear?

answers: The tidings announce an event that will certainly come to pass
The tidings are merely a rumor that will disappear
The tidings describe a past event only
challenge.explanation: The Lord says, “behold, it cometh, and shall be brought to pass.”
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the coming tidings and their fulfillment?

paragraphs.title: The Sword of the King of Babylon

easy.explanation: The sword is sharpened and furbished.
It is sharpened to make a sore slaughter.
Ezekiel is commanded to smite his hands together.
easy.q: What is Ezekiel commanded to do with his hands?

medium.explanation: A furbished sword has been polished so that it may glitter.
medium.q: What does “furbished” mean in the description of the sword?

answers: The Lord’s people and all the princes of Israel
medium.explanation: The sword will be upon the Lord’s people and all the princes of Israel.
medium.q: Who will be affected by the sword?

answers: Because the sword will bring terror upon the people
medium.explanation: He is told to cry and howl because of the terror caused by the sword.
medium.q: Why does Ezekiel cry and howl?

answers: Its readiness and effectiveness for slaughter
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the sword is prepared for deadly action.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by repeating that the sword is sharpened and furbished?

answers: They express intense mourning and alarm
They prevent the sword from being used
challenge.explanation: These actions portray grief and terror at the coming slaughter.
challenge.q: How do crying, howling, and smiting the thigh relate to the sword?

answers: The sword will produce many deaths, including among great men
The sword will protect every slain person
The sword will never reach the city
challenge.explanation: The phrase identifies the sword as one that brings death even into the private chambers of great men.
challenge.q: What does “the sword of the slain” emphasize?

easy.explanation: He is told to appoint two ways for the sword of the king of Babylon to come.
easy.q: How many ways is Ezekiel told to appoint?

easy.explanation: Both ways come forth out of one land.
easy.q: Where do the two ways come forth from?

easy.explanation: One way leads to Judah in Jerusalem.
easy.q: Which city is named as one destination?

answers: Divination, arrows, images, and the liver
medium.explanation: He makes his arrows bright, consults images, and looks in the liver.
medium.q: What methods does the king of Babylon use to choose his way?

answers: A military structure used against a city
medium.explanation: The fort is part of the siege preparations against Jerusalem.
medium.q: What is a “fort” in the context of the siege?

answers: Battering rams and a siege mound
medium.explanation: He plans to appoint battering rams, cast a mount, and build a fort.
medium.q: What does the king plan to appoint against Jerusalem?

answers: They would not understand that it was leading the sword toward them
It had actually prevented the siege
It promised that their sins were forgiven
challenge.explanation: Although they regarded it as false, the divination resulted in Jerusalem being targeted.
challenge.q: Why would the divination appear false to the people of Jerusalem?

answers: Their iniquity is remembered and their transgressions are discovered, so they are taken
Their sins are forgotten, so they escape
challenge.explanation: The passage says their sins appear and that they will therefore be taken.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between sin and capture?

answers: A crossroads, divination, the choice of Jerusalem, and siege preparations
A siege, a coronation, and the destruction of Babylon
A peace treaty, a feast, and a withdrawal
challenge.explanation: The king reaches the crossroads, uses divination, chooses Jerusalem, and prepares the siege.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the events?

paragraphs.title: The Fall of the Prince and the Punishment of Ammon

easy.explanation: The Lord commands, “Remove the diadem, and take off the crown.”
easy.q: What is removed from the prince of Israel?

answers: The low will be exalted and the high will be abased
The high will be exalted and the low forgotten
easy.explanation: The passage announces a reversal of status.
easy.q: What will happen to the order of power?

easy.explanation: The prophecy says, “The sword, the sword is drawn” concerning the Ammonites.
easy.q: What is drawn against the Ammonites?

answers: Until he comes whose right it is
Until the king of Babylon returns home
Until the people rebuild the temple
medium.explanation: The overturning will continue until the rightful ruler comes.
medium.q: Until when will the overturning continue?

answers: A sinful ruler whose day of judgment has come
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the wicked prince of Israel facing judgment.

answers: They trusted vanity and a lying divination
medium.explanation: Their false visions and lying divination are associated with their judgment.
medium.q: Why will the Ammonites face the sword?

answers: The end of the prince’s royal authority
His coronation as a greater king
challenge.explanation: Removing the royal symbols represents the prince’s loss of power.
challenge.q: What does removing the diadem and crown signify?

answers: It strongly emphasizes the complete reversal of the existing order
It promises that the kingdom will never change
challenge.explanation: The repetition highlights the certainty and extent of the political upheaval.
challenge.q: What is the significance of the repeated word “overturn”?

answers: Both are connected with false expectations before judgment
Both are chosen to rule Israel
challenge.explanation: Jerusalem relies on a false divination, while Ammon trusts vanity and a lie; both face judgment.
challenge.q: What similarity exists between Jerusalem and the Ammonites in this passage?
